subject: Quick question about trig functions / angular calculations

messages.author: f5b13b580eb160db
messages.subject: Quick question about trig functions / angular calculations
parts:
Hello,

My apologies if this isn't an appropriate question for the group here - it seems fairly simple but I've done a bit of research and I'm still stumped. I'm writing a model in TMB that includes two parameters x and y; these parameters represent spatial coordinates. I want to calculate the angle created by the coordinate point (x,y) and the x-axis within the TMB likelihood function I'm writing, and I'm not sure about the best way to proceed.

I am aware that this angle is typically calculated using atan(x / y), but this poses two problems for me: a) if y == 0 there are issues, and b) the atan function only returns values between -pi/2 and pi/2, so any angle outside that interval can't be generated. For example, if (x, y) = (2, -1) it will return the same value as if (x, y) = (-2, 1), even though these angles would be very different. Normally I would handle these issues with an "if" statement, but since x and y are parameters I can't do this in TMB without threatening the continuity of the function.

In R there is an atan2(x,y) function that handles these issues and returns an angle within (-pi, pi), and this is something I'd be looking for. However, I can't find it anywhere in the TMB library. Is there a function in TMB I'm missing that can allow me to do this nicely?

Thanks so much in advance for your help,
Peter Thompson

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Quick question about trig functions / angular calculations
parts:
The following works from a TMB template:

PARAMETER(x);
PARAMETER(y);
Type z = atan2(x,y);
